reason: This passage (Exodus 2:11-15) actually demonstrates the opposite of the statement. Moses kills an Egyptian taskmaster and must flee for his life—his violent action is presented as having negative consequences rather than as a model of leadership. The following day, when Moses encounters two Hebrews fighting, he attempts peaceful mediation by questioning the aggressor (לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ - 'Why are you striking your fellow?'), not through violence. The passage portrays violence as a desperate act with serious repercussions, not as a model for effective leadership.
